key_insight: Fu-TCM-27B led six TCM benchmarks, suggesting that structured reasoning supervision can improve automated syndrome differentiation.
clinical_relevance: The model may support research into TCM diagnostic reasoning, but these benchmark results do not establish clinical safety or patient benefit.
method: Trained on cleaned and filtered data from an initial collection of approximately 7.12 million examples.
Combined classical texts, textbooks, medical images, clinical cases and public datasets.
Used Bianzheng-Grounded Policy Optimization to reward response format, intermediate reasoning fields and final syndrome predictions.
evidence_signal: Across six TCM reasoning, text and vision benchmarks, Fu-TCM-27B achieved 81.01% macro-average accuracy, exceeding the strongest reference model with complete results by 7.13 percentage points.
watch_item: The abstract reports benchmark evaluation, not prospective clinical validation; real-world reliability remains unestablished.
paper_title: Fu-TCM: a multimodal large language model that learns traditional Chinese medicine diagnostic reasoning
